concept: TCMalloc zero-rate background release versus allocator-generation units

claims.text: The pinned upstream interface scopes its zero-inhibits-release wording to the background page-heap release path. ProcessBackgroundActions() also performs housekeeping that releases memory from inaccessible CPUs. Thus a zero configured page-heap rate must not be read as disabling every background action; The cited MongoDB release still starts this loop when its background-thread flag and NeedsProcessBackgroundActions() permit it. This is an interface-level explanation, not a measured MongoDB zero-rate release amount. (high confidence)

temporal.applicability_version: MongoDB implementation r8.0.0; Google interface commit 3f041ff383769ae362a3f60dbc3b6a4226abdf8d. The two cited versions are separate; no vendored-commit equivalence or measured MongoDB amount is asserted.

claims.text: The zero-rate background-thread interpretation must be bounded by allocator generation: the MongoDB 8.0 reference says tcmalloc-gperf platforms, including Windows, PPC and s390x, retain earlier tcmallocReleaseRate behavior. In the cited MongoDB release, startAllocatorThread() implements the background loop only under MONGO_CONFIG_TCMALLOC_GOOGLE; the other compile-time branch does nothing. Enabling the parameter therefore does not establish that this Google allocator background loop exists on a gperf build. (high confidence)

Attributed positions in the cited documentation: the manual Markdown’s general tcmallocReleaseRate=0 sentence says MongoDB does not return memory; its tcmallocEnableBackgroundThread=true and tcmallocReleaseRate=0 note says that MongoDB still releases memory. The MongoDB 8.0 parameter reference explicitly states this conditional background-thread exception for the Google-TCMalloc path and describes possible release near the heap limit and from intermediate caches. In the cited MongoDB release, the Google-allocator thread-start code checks the background-thread flag and NeedsProcessBackgroundActions(), but does not test tcmallocReleaseRate before invoking ProcessBackgroundActions(). These are attributed documentation positions and a scoped code path, not two unconditional runtime conclusions or a promise of a measured release amount. (high confidence)

temporal.applicability_version: MongoDB 8.0 parameter reference and r8.0.0 Google-allocator implementation; cited manual body is a separately hash-bound documentation snapshot. The conflicting source positions are attributed, not resolved into an unconditional runtime promise.
